description: The Fire Dog in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1946 and 2006 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Dog is the Dog born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the eleventh animal. It combines the Dog's loyalty with Fire's qualities. Fire Dog years between 1924 and 2044 are 1946 and 2006. The Dog's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Fire Dog personality
paragraphs: Fire generates Earth, and the Dog always carries Earth, so a Fire year is said to warm and strengthen this loyal animal, adding passion and confidence to its sense of duty. Fire Dogs are often described as energetic, honest and courageous, ready to fight for what they believe and protect those they love. They tend to be charismatic and outspoken, with strong convictions. Their loyalty, once given, burns brightly. The added heat can also make them impulsive or quick to anger when they sense injustice, and readings mention a tendency to take on battles that are not theirs to fight, or to judge harshly when someone falls short. Their protectiveness can be fierce, but it is rarely selfish.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: Fire Dog at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

Champion of the underdog is the role tradition hands the Fire Dog. Activism, firefighting, employment law, campaigning journalism and youth coaching are frequently named, because courage and conviction carry real weight in each. It gives everything to a cause it believes in and expects colleagues to be straight with it; office spin or quiet favouritism can provoke a memorable outburst. In love the Fire Dog is ardent and loyal, the partner who will drive across the country at midnight if something goes wrong. Shared principles matter more to it than shared hobbies. Where things go awry is righteous anger: a perceived unfairness, even a small one, may ignite an argument out of all proportion to the original slight.

sections.heading: Fire Dog years and dates
paragraphs: The table from 1924 to 2044 holds 2 Fire Dog years: 1946, starting Feb 2 and 2006, starting Jan 29. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1946 anyone born before Feb 2 is a Wood Rooster, not a Fire Dog. It takes sixty years for the Fire stem and the Dog branch to coincide again, which is why the same pairing marks grandparents and grandchildren rather than siblings. Every Fire Dog year is Yang, matching the Dog's own polarity.

In the sexagenary calendar this is the Bing-Xu year, the Fire stem Bing with the Dog's branch Xu. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Rooster year (before February 2, 1946) and the Wood Rooster year (before January 29, 2006), and births in the weeks after each Fire Dog year ends belong to the Fire Pig. The new year itself fell on a Saturday in 1946 and Sunday in 2006.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Dog
paragraphs: Fire Dogs tend to grow by choosing their battles wisely. Asking whether a fight is theirs, and whether it can be won, conserves their considerable energy for causes that truly matter. Pausing before reacting to perceived unfairness prevents regrettable words. Fire Dogs often thrive in advocacy, emergency services or leadership roles, where courage and loyalty are valued. Physical activity helps release tension that builds when they feel wronged. Extending grace to people who disappoint them deepens relationships. When passion is channelled with judgement, Fire Dogs become steadfast and inspiring protectors.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Dog shares the Dog's San He trine with the Tiger and Horse (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Rabbit, and its Liu Chong clash with the Dragon. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Dog years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1946 (from February 2, 1946) and 2006 (from January 29, 2006). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Dog's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Dog's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles fire generates Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Dog?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Tiger and Horse (San He) and the Rabbit (Liu He). The Dragon is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Dog called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Bing-Xu. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Bing, followed by its earthly branch, here Xu for the Dog, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Dog different from other Dogs?
faq.answer: All Dogs share loyalty, fairness and protectiveness. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
